title: test_protocol_vector_security.py: root-binding biconditional conflates binding failure with admission failure
description: From xszc codereview pass 1 (correctness, reviewer kimi-k3): python/tests/test_protocol_vector_security.py:361-363 asserts 'root_binding is (vector["expected"]["admitted"] is True)'. This holds for the current authenticated_schc_dio.json corpus only because every non-admitted root vector also carries a non-binding DODAGID. A future root vector rejected for a non-binding reason (e.g., SCHC version mismatch, wrong role scope with a CORRECT DODAGID) while admitted=False would break the assertion even though binding itself is fine. Pre-existing structure (not introduced by the xszc one-line flip). Fix shape: split into two assertions — binding check applies only where the vector isolates binding (e.g., gate on an explicit vector field like expected.binding_valid), or assert binding == (admitted is True) only for vectors whose rejection stage is dodag binding. P3 test-robustness.
